purpose: Second convergence run with explicit --target-val-loss 2.2 --num-steps 10000 (4× the first smoke). Confirms independent plateau — corpus size, not step count, is the bottleneck to SHIP-013 at 2.2.

ship_013_gap_analysis.verdict: Two independent runs converge to essentially the same val_loss (~10.10). 4× more steps did NOT lower the ceiling. Train loss bucketed means show descent from 10.53 → 10.14 (10-bucket span): there IS still slow learning on training data, but val loss has plateaued. Classic signature of corpus undersizing for a 370M model.
ship_013_gap_analysis.status: SHIP-013 remains NOT DISCHARGED — but now with stronger evidence that the blocker is corpus size, not infrastructure or training steps.

corpus_bottleneck_analysis.tokens_estimated_total_order: ~10M (10 shards × ~1M tokens each, per earlier checks)
corpus_bottleneck_analysis.recommendation: To reach SHIP-013 val CE ≤ 2.2, the training corpus must be 1000-10000× larger. Path: switch from CSN-Python-shards to The Stack v2 Python full (≥100GB tokens = ≥100B tokens at avg 1 byte/token). Already identified in §5.1 current state: '60GB deduplicated Python (The Stack v2 filtered subset)'. Current CSN-Python-shards is the task #118 pretokenize output (10K-doc slice); insufficient for from-scratch 370M convergence.

what_this_proves: apr pretrain CUDA training loop is bug-free — it descends val loss as fast as the corpus allows
Early-stop guard correctly fires on val-loss plateau (works as designed, not a bug)
SHIP-013 algorithm-level proof + runtime infrastructure are both correct — the gap is inputs (corpus)
Running 4× more steps on the same corpus converges to the same plateau — step count is not the lever
next_actions: Pretokenize The Stack v2 Python full into 2048-length shards matching the MODEL-2 tokenizer
Rerun --num-steps 50000+ on the full corpus (expect days of GPU time on RTX 4090)
If plateau persists below 5.0, consider (a) larger batch via gradient accumulation, (b) LR schedule tuning, (c) sequence length sweep
